title: page-siloing-locality-preserving-evictor-and-spill-attenuation
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Introduces page siloing and a locality-preserving evictor to reduce fragmentation and spill I/O; adds adaptive spill attenuation knobs and telemetry; no API changes.
description: Context: Our KV cache has increasing fragmentation and frequent small spill writes under mixed workloads (short chat traces + occasional long contexts). Motivation: reduce tail latency and spill I/O amplification by keeping hot keys co-located in contiguous page 'silos' and by making the evictor prefer locality-preserving demotions. This PR implements a page siloing allocator, a locality-preserving eviction policy, and a spill attenuation controller that defers and coalesces spill writes when under transient pressure. Changes are gated behind a runtime flag (kv.page_siloing_enabled) and incremental by default. Design summary: 1) Page siloing allocator groups allocations into silos by tenant and affinity score computed from recent access fingerprinting. Silos aim to keep related KV entries on contiguous page ranges to reduce fragmentation and sequentialize spill write patterns. 2) Locality-preserving evictor selects victims not only by recency/heat but also by silo contiguity score so evictions prefer reclaiming whole subranges that yield contiguous free segments. This substantially reduces micro-fragmentation. 3) Spill attenuation controller monitors spill sink bandwidth and in-flight spill latency; when spikes occur it switches from immediate per-page spill to deferred coalesced-write mode (batching multiple evicted pages into a single larger write, limited by a configurable max_coalesce_bytes). 4) Integration with scheduler: the evictor now exposes a hint to the continuous-batching scheduler so that inflight generation batches avoid pinning tokens to pages that are being reclaimed, reducing KV lookup latency spikes during concurrent eviction. 5) Telemetry and evaluation: new metrics (kv.silo_fill_ratio, kv.eviction_contiguity, kv.spill_coalesce_ratio) and an end-to-end perf test harness that simulates mixed short+long context traffic. Implementation notes: - New package/runtime files: kv/silo_allocator.{cc,hh}, kv/evictor_locality.cc, kv/spill_attenuator.cc, scheduler/evictor_hints.go - Conservative default config: silo max size = 8MB, coalesce window = 50ms, max_coalesce_bytes = 2MB - Backwards compatible: no public API changes, feature off by default. Migration path: customers can enable per-tenant via console or feature flags; rollout plan includes dark launches and Canary pool in Dedicated. Test plan: unit tests for silo placement, fuzz tests for contiguity heuristics, integration perf job in perf-canary (redwood/perf-canary) comparing tail latency and WAN spill traffic. CI: initial CI run failed on an intermittent scheduler race in continuous batching; fixed by adding a small handshake between evictor and scheduler (evictor_hints now uses a version token to ensure stale hints are ignored). Outcomes: synthetic perf runs show 18-28% reduction in spill IOPS for mixed workloads and 6-12% tail latency improvement (95th/99th) in our canary environment. Risk/Tradeoffs: - Coalescing spikes into larger writes increases latency of reclaim path under sustained pressure; attenuation controller uses conservative defaults to avoid unbounded backlog. - Siloing increases internal fragmentation risk for extremely small tenant workloads; mitigated by letting small tenants share silos until threshold. Related: follows patterns from ENG-2143 and borrows parts of earlier spill-backpressure work (SUP-4021).

review_comments: Marco DeLuca: Nice work. Can you quantify memory overhead for silo metadata? Also please ensure the allocator path is hot-path optimized (avoid locks).

Priya Natarajan: Silo metadata is ~128 bytes per active silo; silos are sized to amortize metadata. Hot path uses a lock-free fastpath (see silo_allocator.h comment) and falling back to a per-thread slab under contention.
Lina Zhao: The contiguity score looks promising but I'm concerned about tenant fairness—could a noisy tenant hog contiguous pages?
Priya Natarajan: Added a tenant-share cap and a decay on affinity score; documented in configs/kv_default.yaml and added unit test 'tenant_share_cap_test'.
Owen Park: CI reported a flake in continuous-batcher when evictor hints were delayed. Did you add ordering guarantees?
Priya Natarajan: Yes — added a version token in evictor_hints; scheduler ignores hints with older tokens. This resolved the flake (see commit 9f8e7d6).
Marco DeLuca: Approving pending squash and a short perf run on the canary cluster.
Lina Zhao: Observability looks adequate; approve after addressing small doc nits.
Automation Bot: CLA and license checks passed.
